result:
These queries come from the documentation page alone and none were run. Several assumptions could break them:
- The `sort` key `~([(/n | desc) /name])` is taken as given.
- `unionOf` is assumed to work on two plain maps in T8.
- A trailing blank line may make `lines` produce an empty string, so T10 reads the level with `at 1` and T12 and T13 drop short rows with `count | gt 1`.

T1: /data/users | filter ~(/active) | filter ~(at :email | coalesce "" | lower | endsWith "@example.com") | count
T2: /data/users | filter ~(/roles * lower | any ~(eq "admin")) | sort ~(/name | lower) * /name
T3: /data/users | groupBy ~(at :profile | coalesce {} | at :country | coalesce "unknown") * count
T4: /data/users * (at :profile | coalesce {} | at :age) | filter ~(ne null) | avg | round 2
T5: filter ~(/state | eq "open") * /labels | flat | * (/name | lower) | distinct | sort
T6: sort ~([(/comments | desc) /number]) | take 3 * {:number /number :assignee (at :assignee | coalesce {} | at :login)}
T7: filter ~(/state | eq "open") | filter ~(at :assignee | ne null) | groupBy ~(/assignee/login) * count
T8: unionOf /dependencies /devDependencies | entries | filter ~(/1 | startsWith "^") | sort ~(/0) * ([(/0 | keyword) "@" /1] | join "")
T9: /services | filter ~(at :enabled | eq true) | filter ~(/port | gt 8000) * (/name | lower) | sort | join ","
T10: lines * split " " | filter ~(at 1 | eq "ERROR") | groupBy ~(/2) * count
T11: lines * (split " " | filter ~(startsWith "ms=")) | filter ~(count | gt 0) * (/0 | drop 3 | parseJson) | avg | round 1
T12: lines | drop 1 * split "," | filter ~(count | gt 1) | filter ~(/5 | lower | eq "shipped") | filter ~(/4 | ne "") * (mulOf (/3 | parseJson) (/4 | parseJson)) | sum | round 2
T13: lines | drop 1 * split "," | filter ~(count | gt 1) | filter ~(/5 | lower | ne "cancelled") | filter ~(/4 | ne "") * {:customer /1 :total (mulOf (/3 | parseJson) (/4 | parseJson))} | groupBy ~(/customer) * {:customer (first | /customer) :total (* /total | sum | round 2)} | vals | sort ~(/total | desc) | take 2
T14: ["Banana" "apple" "Cherry" "banana" "fig" "APPLE" "date" "kiwi" "Fig" "elderberry"] * lower | distinct | sort ~([(count | desc) /]) | join "-"
